offer.artBody: Most signage vendors deliver one mp4. If the next lobby is 1:6 instead of 16:9, that file is wrong. We write a deterministic piece: the same seed on the same canvas always draws the same picture, then we print it at the site ratio. Public APIs or an institution’s database can drive color, density, or motion when a live picture is wanted. If you only need a beautiful loop, we still deliver 4K video that drops onto the player you already own.

offer.ledBody: We size, supply, and install lobby media walls, building-face LED, and vertical signage — including structure, cabling, and power. If a panel is already on the wall, we match its resolution and input and change only the content.
offer.facadeBody: We survey the wall, choose projector count and brightness, map around windows and columns, and run dusk-timed playback. Festival and opening-week installs include take-down. Daytime or short-throw sites that cannot hold a projector are usually better as LED — we say so after the survey.

home.a: A media facade treats a building face as a display — either LED built into the architecture or projection mapped onto the wall. Public Bloom (오늘은 봄날) produces the media art and can install the hardware in one contract, so you do not brief a content studio and an electrician separately. The public site is publicbloom.art.

home.q: Can I buy media art for an LED I already have?
home.a: Yes. Open Media Art AX (Bomnal Studio) without an account, preview a screen, then we render to your aspect ratio and resolution. If the panel is already on the wall, an HDMI media box is often enough. Weekday file delivery is within 24 hours after you confirm.

home.q: Do you only work in Korea?
home.a: The studio is in Daegu. Installed sites are mainly Daegu, Busan, and Gyeongbuk, with Gyeongnam and Ulsan by arrangement. International buyers: we discuss remote content delivery first. Installation outside those Korean regions is case by case — we do not claim a worldwide install service.

LED in the architecture is a physical screen that can run in daylight. Projection mapping is light fitted to an existing surface, usually at night. Both are in scope when the site fits. We recommend after looking at the wall, ambient light, throw distance, and power.

offer.a: A media facade uses a building exterior or gallery wall as one large image. 오늘은 봄날 typically does this with projectors and projection mapping: the picture is warped to windows, columns, and cornices instead of hanging a new screen. Night festivals, openings, and indoor monumental walls are the usual fit.

offer.q: Do I need a new LED if I already have a panel?
offer.a: No. Existing lobby walls, outdoor boards, and information totems can keep their hardware. The studio matches resolution and input and supplies new media-art content. A survey still checks viewing distance, brightness, and power before the spec is locked.

offer.q: Can institutional data appear on the screen?
offer.a: Yes, when the values are numeric or scheduled — visitors, energy, bookings, air quality, notices. Public APIs can be read live; in-house databases are connected through a relay that follows the institution’s security rules. The result is color, particles, and motion, not a spreadsheet on the wall.

Published prices, VAT excluded: one work KRW 1,000,000; four seasonal works KRW 3,900,000; ten custom works in a year KRW 9,000,000. Installation of LED or projectors is not in those figures and is quoted after a site survey.

studio.q: Do I pay inside the studio?
studio.a: Not yet. The studio is for choosing a look. Purchase and invoicing happen by email quote. Individuals and institutions both write to studio@publicbloom.art.

Usually a 4K mp4 cropped to your panel. If the screen should change with weather or data, you receive live code that runs on a player the studio can configure. If there is no screen, installation of LED or projectors can be added to the same conversation.

studio.q: The studio UI is in Korean. Can I still use it?
studio.a: Yes. You are choosing pictures, palettes, and motion — not writing Korean copy. If you prefer not to use the editor, send a reference image and request three concepts. This English page exists so the offer is clear before you open the tool.

quote.q: Do you accept work from outside Korea?
quote.a: Yes. Remote content commissions are routine. Describe the city, the screen, and the deadline. Installation travel outside Daegu–Busan–Gyeongbuk–Gyeongnam–Ulsan is discussed per project.

quote.q: What should the first email include?
quote.a: Organization name, a reachable email, wall or panel size (or a photo), and whether you need content only, hardware, or both. Budget range is optional. The more specific the brief, the tighter the first concepts.

For Korean government and foundation buyers, the studio issues fiscal-year quotes plus the women-owned and direct-production certificates on request. Foreign institutional purchase orders are handled by email.
